subject: math
title: Algebraic Expressions: Evaluating, Simplifying, Polynomials, and Factoring
objectives: You will translate word phrases into algebraic expressions and write real-life formulas for cost and perimeter.
You will evaluate algebraic expressions for given values, including negative numbers and exponents.
You will simplify expressions by combining like terms and using the distributive property.
You will add, subtract, and multiply polynomials, including squares of binomials.
You will factor expressions using the greatest common factor, trinomial factoring, and the difference of squares.

slides.title: Week 7 Math: Algebraic Expressions
slides.board:
Algebraic Expressions

Evaluating, Simplifying, Polynomials, and Factoring

  • Turn words into expressions and real-life formulas
  • Evaluate expressions, including negatives and exponents
  • Simplify with like terms and the distributive property
  • Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials
  • Factor: GCF, trinomials, difference of squares

Today: warm-up, five skills (teach, example, together, on your own), two GED-style questions, one strategy

notes.say: Welcome to Week 7. This is where the GED math test turns into algebra, and about half of the test is algebra. Every skill today is a tool you will use again in equations next week, graphs the week after, and quadratics in Week 10. Letters in math are just numbers we have not named yet, so every rule you learned about numbers in Week 1 still works. Keep your paper ready: we will write every step.
ask: When you see a letter like x in a math problem, how do you feel about it on a scale of 1 to 5? (expected answer: any; use it to decide how slowly to take the first two concepts)
notes.watch: Pacing for 60 minutes: warm-up 5 min (slide 2); words and evaluating 11 min (slides 3–8); like terms and distributing 11 min (slides 9–13); polynomials 13 min (slides 14–19); factoring 15 min (slides 20–25); strategy and recap 5 min (slides 26–27). If you run short on time, cut the we-do slides to two problems each, but never skip factoring: it carries straight into Week 10.

slides.title: Warm-up: Last Week in Four Problems
slides.board:
Review of Week 6 (volume, surface area, scale). Use the formula sheet; calculator allowed.

  1. Volume of a box 8 cm long, 5 cm wide, 3 cm tall
  2. Volume of a cylinder with radius 3 in and height 10 in (use 3.14 for π)
  3. Scale 1 in : 12 ft. A wall is 4.5 in long on the plan. Actual length?
  4. Surface area of a cube with 5 cm edges
steps: Notice: every formula you used is an algebraic expression. Putting numbers in for the letters is called evaluating. That is today’s first skill.

notes.say: Take about three minutes. These are last week’s skills, and every one of them is secretly today’s skill too. A formula like V = lwh is an expression with letters; when you put in 8, 5, and 3, you evaluated it. Tell me your answers one at a time.
ask: In number 2, what did you square: the radius or the radius times π? (expected answer: only the radius; 3<sup>2</sup> = 9, then multiply by 3.14 and 10)
What is the difference between volume and surface area? (expected answer: volume fills the inside, in cubic units; surface area covers the outside, in square units)
notes.watch: On number 2, 3.14 × 3 × 2 × 10 = 188.4 means the student doubled the radius instead of squaring it; on number 4, 125 means the student found volume (5<sup>3</sup>) instead of surface area. Both are the same habit we fix today: read the expression exactly as written.

slides.title: Words into Expressions
slides.board:
A variable is a letter that stands for a number. An expression uses numbers, variables, and operations. No equal sign.

OperationKey wordsExample
+sum, more than, increased by, total8 more than n → n + 8
−difference, less than, decreased by5 less than n → n − 5
×product, times, twice, oftwice n → 2n
÷quotient, per, divided by, splitn split 4 ways → n/4

Cost = flat fee + rate × amount

notes.say: Algebra is a language, and translating is the first skill. Most key words go in the order you read them, with one big exception: “less than” flips. Five less than n means you start with n and take 5 away, so n − 5. Also watch grouping words: “twice the sum of n and 3” is 2(n + 3), because you find the sum first. And most real-life bills follow one pattern: a flat fee you pay once plus a rate times how much you use.
ask: Write “5 less than n” and test it with n = 20. (expected answer: n − 5; 20 − 5 = 15, and 5 less than 20 really is 15)
What is the difference between “twice the sum of n and 3” and “the sum of twice n and 3”? (expected answer: 2(n + 3) versus 2n + 3)
notes.watch: Students write 5 − n for “5 less than n.” Fix it with a real number every time: 5 less than 20 is 15, and 5 − 20 is −15, so 5 − n cannot be right.

slides.title: Writing and Using a Cost Formula
slides.board:
A truck rental costs $29.95 plus $0.79 per mile.

(a) Write an expression for the cost of driving d miles.

(b) Find the cost of a 120-mile trip.
steps: Fixed part (paid once): 29.95. Variable part (depends on miles): 0.79d.
Trap: (29.95 + 0.79) × 120 = $3,688.80 charges the flat fee for every mile. Does that make sense for one truck? No.

notes.say: Sort every cost problem into two piles: what you pay once, and what you pay per unit. The per-unit part always has the variable attached. When you evaluate, multiplication comes before addition, so the rate times the miles happens first, and then you add the flat fee.
ask: Which number gets the variable, and why? (expected answer: 0.79, because that charge depends on the number of miles)
notes.watch: If the student adds 29.95 + 0.79 first, ask: “How many times do you pay the $29.95?” Once, so it cannot be multiplied by 120.

slides.title: Translating Together
slides.board:
Write an expression for each.

  1. 7 less than a number n
  2. The quotient of a number n and 4, increased by 3
  3. Three times the difference of a number n and 2
  4. A phone plan: $35 a month plus $10 for each extra line, L extra lines
steps: 3. “The difference” is a group, so it goes in parentheses: 3(n − 2)

notes.say: Let’s do these together. For each one, tell me the key word first, then the expression. I will reveal one line at a time. Number 3 is the one to slow down on: the word “difference” makes a group, and a group needs parentheses.
ask: In number 3, why do we need parentheses? (expected answer: we multiply the whole difference by 3, not just n)
In number 4, what is the cost with 2 extra lines? (expected answer: 35 + 10(2) = $55)
notes.watch: 7 − n on number 1 is the “less than” flip; 3n − 2 on number 3 is missing parentheses (test n = 5: three times the difference of 5 and 2 is 9, and 3(5) − 2 = 13).

slides.title: Evaluating Expressions
slides.board:
Evaluate = find the value. Two steps:

  1. Substitute each number in parentheses.
  2. Follow the order of operations: grouping, exponents, × and ÷, + and −.
If x = −3Value
x2 = (−3)29
−x2 = −(−3)2−9
5x = 5(−3)−15
4 − x = 4 − (−3)7

5xy means 5 × x × y.

notes.say: Evaluating is the most common algebra task on the GED, and almost every mistake comes from one habit: dropping parentheses. When x is −3, x squared is negative 3 times negative 3, which is positive 9. If you write −3 squared without parentheses, the calculator and the order of operations both read it as the negative of 9. So the rule is simple: every substituted number goes in parentheses, every time.
ask: If x = −3, what is −x<sup>2</sup>? (expected answer: −9; square first to get 9, then take the negative)
If x = −3, what is 4 − x? (expected answer: 4 − (−3) = 7)
notes.watch: On the TI-30XS, (−3)<sup>2</sup> must be entered with the parentheses and the (−) key. Typing (−) 3 x<sup>2</sup> without parentheses gives −9.

slides.title: Evaluating with Two Variables
slides.board: Evaluate 2x2 − 5xy + y when x = −3 and y = 2.

notes.say: Watch how carefully I copy the expression with parentheses before doing any math. That one line of rewriting is where the points are won. Then it is just Week 1: exponents, then multiplying, then adding and subtracting from left to right.
ask: What would you get if you squared −3 as −9? (expected answer: 2(−9) = −18, then −18 + 30 + 2 = 14; a wrong answer)
notes.watch: Two traps here: (−3)<sup>2</sup> written as −9, and 18 − (−30) written as 18 − 30. Have the student say “minus a negative is plus” out loud.

slides.title: Your Turn: Translate and Evaluate
slides.board:
Three minutes. Work on paper.

  1. Write: 6 less than twice a number n
  2. Evaluate 4a − 3b when a = 5 and b = −2
  3. Evaluate x2 + 3x when x = −4
  4. Evaluate −x2 + 10 when x = 3

notes.say: Your turn. I am starting the clock for three minutes. Write the substitution line with parentheses before you compute anything; I will ask to see it. When time is up, read me your four answers.
ask: Read me your answers. (expected answer: 2n − 6, 26, 4, 1)
notes.watch: 14 on number 2 means 20 − 6 (the sign of b was lost). −28 on number 3 means (−4)<sup>2</sup> was taken as −16. 19 on number 4 means the student squared −3 instead of taking the negative of 3<sup>2</sup>.

slides.title: Terms, Coefficients, and Like Terms
slides.board:
Terms are separated by + and − signs. The sign belongs to the term.

TermCoefficientVariable part
5x25x2
−3x−3x
y1y
7(constant)none

Like terms have the same variable part, exponents included. Combine them by adding the coefficients.

7x − 2x = 5x    3x + 2 stays    3x and 3x2 are not like terms

notes.say: Think of like terms as the same kind of item. Seven apples minus two apples is five apples, but three apples plus two dollars is still three apples plus two dollars. x and x squared are different items, so they never combine. When you combine, only the coefficient changes; the variable part stays exactly the same.
ask: Are 4xy and −9yx like terms? (expected answer: yes; xy and yx are the same product)
Simplify 7x + 3y − 2x + 5 − 4y. (expected answer: 5x − y + 5)
notes.watch: Students write 2x + 3x<sup>2</sup> = 5x<sup>3</sup> or 3x + 2 = 5x. Color-code or circle each kind of term; only terms of the same color combine.

slides.title: The Distributive Property
slides.board:
a(b + c) = ab + ac   Multiply the outside number by every term inside, signs included.

3(x + 4)3x + 12
−2(x − 5)−2x + 10
−(x − 7)−x + 7
x(x + 6)x2 + 6x

A minus sign in front of parentheses is a −1 that flips every sign inside.

notes.say: The distributive property says the outside number visits everyone inside the parentheses. Draw an arrow from the outside number to each term inside so nobody gets skipped. The sign in front of the parentheses goes along with the number: negative 2 times negative 5 is positive 10. A minus sign alone in front of parentheses is really negative 1, so it flips every sign inside.
ask: Distribute −4(2x − 3). (expected answer: −8x + 12)
What is −(x − 7)? (expected answer: −x + 7)
notes.watch: The two classic errors are 3(x + 4) = 3x + 4 (only the first term) and −2(x − 5) = −2x − 10 (the sign of the second product). Ask the student to read each product aloud: “negative two times negative five.”

slides.title: Distribute, Then Combine
slides.board: Simplify: 4(2x − 3) − 2(x − 5)
steps: Answer: 6x − 2. Check with x = 1: 4(−1) − 2(−4) = −4 + 8 = 4, and 6(1) − 2 = 4. They match.

notes.say: Two moves, always in this order: distribute, then combine. I treat the minus sign in front of the 2 as part of the number, so I am distributing negative 2. Then I gather like terms. At the end, I check by plugging in a small number into both the original and my answer. If they match, I can trust it.
ask: Why is the last product +10 and not −10? (expected answer: −2 × −5 is positive)
notes.watch: If the student gets 6x − 22, they wrote −2(x − 5) as −2x − 10. If they get 10x − 2, they added 8x + 2x.

slides.title: Simplifying Together
slides.board:
Simplify each expression.

  1. 9y + 4 − 3y − 10
  2. 5(x + 2) − 3x + 4
  3. 6 − 2(3x − 4) + x
  4. 3(a + 2b) − (a − b)

notes.say: Let’s do these together. Tell me the distributing line first, then the combining line. Number 3 is the most important one: the 6 in front is not multiplied by anything. The −2 belongs to the parentheses only.
ask: In number 3, a student wrote 4(3x − 4) + x. What went wrong? (expected answer: they subtracted 6 − 2 first; distributing comes before subtracting)
In number 4, what happens to −b inside the second parentheses? (expected answer: the minus sign in front flips it to +b)
notes.watch: On number 3, 13x − 16 means the student computed 6 − 2 = 4 first. On number 4, 2a + 5b means the minus sign flipped only the a.

slides.title: GED-Style Question: Equivalent Expressions
slides.board:
Which expression is equivalent to 7 − 3(2x − 5)?

A. 8x − 20    B. −6x − 8    C. −6x + 22    D. −6x + 2
steps: Eliminate A (8x − 20): it comes from subtracting 7 − 3 = 4 first, then 4(2x − 5). Distributing comes before subtracting.
Eliminate B (−6x − 8): it comes from −3 × (−5) = −15. A negative times a negative is positive.
Eliminate D (−6x + 2): it comes from distributing to only the first term: 7 − 6x − 5.
C (−6x + 22) is correct: −3 × 2x = −6x, −3 × (−5) = +15, so 7 − 6x + 15 = −6x + 22. Check x = 1: 7 − 3(−3) = 16 and −6 + 22 = 16.

notes.say: Here is a real GED format: “Which expression is equivalent?” Every wrong choice is built from one of the mistakes we just practiced. Solve it first, then use the plug-in check: pick x = 1 or 2, evaluate the original, and see which choice matches.
ask: Which choice did you pick, and what was your distributing line? (expected answer: C; 7 − 6x + 15)
notes.watch: If the student chose A, go back to the order of operations: multiplication (distributing) before subtraction. If B, read the product −3 × −5 aloud.

slides.title: Polynomials: Add and Subtract
slides.board:
A polynomial is one term or a sum of terms with whole-number exponents.

Monomial (1 term)5x2
Binomial (2 terms)x + 4
Trinomial (3 terms)x2 + 3x − 2

Standard form: highest exponent first.

Add: drop the parentheses, combine like terms.
Subtract: flip the sign of every term in the second polynomial, then combine.

notes.say: Polynomials are just longer expressions, so you already know how to work with them: combine like terms. Adding is easy. Subtracting is where most points are lost, because the minus sign in front of the second polynomial is really a negative 1 being distributed. That means every single term inside changes sign, not just the first one. Rewrite the second polynomial with flipped signs before you combine anything.
ask: How many terms does 4x<sup>3</sup> − x + 9 have, and what is it called? (expected answer: three; a trinomial)
What is −(x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 4)? (expected answer: −x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 4)
notes.watch: The most common error is flipping only the first sign: −(x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 4) written as −x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 4. Insist on a rewrite line.

slides.title: Subtracting Polynomials
slides.board: Simplify: (3x2 + 2x − 7) − (x2 − 5x + 4)
steps: Flip every sign in the second polynomial: 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 7 − x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 4

notes.say: I write the flip line before anything else. Then I sweep through by type: squares, then x terms, then plain numbers. Lining up like terms in columns also works well if you like a vertical layout.
ask: What would you get if you flipped only the x<sup>2</sup> sign? (expected answer: 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 3, which is wrong)
notes.watch: A student who gets 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 3 flipped only the first term. A student who gets 4x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 3 added the polynomials.

slides.title: Multiplying Polynomials
slides.board:
Every term times every term. Multiply coefficients; add exponents: x × x = x2, 3x × 2x2 = 6x3.

Two binomials: FOIL = First, Outer, Inner, Last — or use a box.

×x+4
3x3x212x
−2−2x−8

(x + 4)(3x − 2) = 3x2 + 12x − 2x − 8 = 3x2 + 10x − 8

notes.say: Multiplying is the distributive property done more than once. Each term in the first group shakes hands with each term in the second group. For two binomials that is four handshakes, and FOIL is just a way to remember all four. The box does the same thing and works for longer polynomials too: put one factor across the top, the other down the side, fill each cell, and combine like terms.
ask: What is 4x × 5x? (expected answer: 20x<sup>2</sup>)
What is 2x(x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 5)? (expected answer: 2x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 10x)
notes.watch: Students often write x × x = 2x. Remind them: x + x = 2x, but x × x = x<sup>2</sup>.

slides.title: Two Binomials and a Square
slides.board:
(a) Multiply (2x − 3)(x + 5)

(b) Multiply (x + 3)2
steps: (a) First 2x × x = 2x<sup>2</sup>; Outer 2x × 5 = 10x; Inner −3 × x = −3x; Last −3 × 5 = −15
(b) Write the square as a product: (x + 3)(x + 3)
Trap: (x + 3)2 is not x2 + 9. Check x = 1: (1 + 3)2 = 16, and 1 + 6 + 9 = 16, but 1 + 9 = 10.

notes.say: Part (b) is the trap the GED loves. Squaring means multiplying the binomial by itself, so there are four products, not two. The two middle products are what people forget. Any time you see a binomial squared, write it out twice.
ask: What is (x − 5)<sup>2</sup>? (expected answer: x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 25)
notes.watch: If the student writes x<sup>2</sup> + 9, have them plug in x = 1 into both forms; the mismatch convinces them better than a rule.

slides.title: Polynomials Together
slides.board:
1. (2x2 − x + 3) + (x2 + 4x − 9)
  2. 2x(x2 − 3x + 5)
  3. (x − 6)(x + 6)
  4. (2x + 1)(x − 4)

notes.say: Let’s work these together. For the products, name each of the four handshakes as you go. Number 3 is special: the middle terms cancel. Remember that pattern; we will run it backward when we factor.
ask: Why does the middle term disappear in number 3? (expected answer: +6x and −6x add to zero)
notes.watch: On number 2, 2x<sup>2</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 10x (or −4x<sup>2</sup> + 10x) means x × x<sup>2</sup> was written as x<sup>2</sup>; exponents add, so it is x<sup>3</sup>. On number 4, 2x<sup>2</sup> − 9x − 4 means the inner product (1 × x = +x) was given the wrong sign.

slides.title: Your Turn: Polynomials
slides.board:
Four minutes.

  1. (4x2 + 3x − 1) − (x2 − 2x + 6)
  2. (x + 3)(x − 7)
  3. (x − 5)2
  4. 3x(2x − 4)

notes.say: Your turn: four minutes. Write the flip line on number 1 and the four products on numbers 2 and 3. Then read me your answers.
ask: Read me your four answers. (expected answer: 3x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 7; x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 21; x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 25; 6x<sup>2</sup> − 12x)
notes.watch: 3x<sup>2</sup> + x + 5 on number 1 means only the first sign was flipped. x<sup>2</sup> + 25 or x<sup>2</sup> − 25 on number 3 means the student squared term by term.

slides.title: Factoring, Step 1: The GCF
slides.board:
Factoring = multiplying in reverse. Write the expression as a product.

Greatest common factor (GCF): the largest number and highest power of each variable that divide every term.

8x3 + 12x2: GCF of 8 and 12 is 4; lowest power of x is x2 → GCF = 4x2

Divide each term: 8x3 ÷ 4x2 = 2x and 12x2 ÷ 4x2 = 3

8x3 + 12x2 = 4x2(2x + 3)   Check: distribute back.

notes.say: Factoring is the distributive property in reverse. Instead of handing the outside number to every term, we pull out what every term has in common. Always look for a GCF first; it makes everything after it easier. And you never have to guess whether a factoring is right: multiply it back out. If you get the original, you are done.
ask: What is the GCF of 6x<sup>2</sup> and 9x? (expected answer: 3x)
Factor 5x<sup>2</sup> + 15x. (expected answer: 5x(x + 3))
notes.watch: Students stop too early: 12x<sup>3</sup> − 18x<sup>2</sup> = 3x<sup>2</sup>(4x − 6) still has a common factor of 2 inside. Ask: “Do the terms inside the parentheses still share a factor?” The full answer is 6x<sup>2</sup>(2x − 3).

slides.title: Trinomials and Difference of Squares
slides.board:
x2 + bx + c: find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.

Signs in the trinomialThe two numbers
c positive, b positiveboth positive
c positive, b negativeboth negative
c negativeopposite signs

Difference of squares: a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b)

x2 − 49 = (x + 7)(x − 7). A sum x2 + 49 does not factor this way.

notes.say: For a trinomial with a leading 1, you are hunting for a pair of numbers: their product is the last number and their sum is the middle number. List the factor pairs of c in a column and add each pair until one gives b. The sign table saves time. For a difference of squares, look for two perfect squares with a minus sign between them; it is exactly the pattern we saw when the middle terms canceled.
ask: Two numbers multiply to 12 and add to 7. What are they? (expected answer: 3 and 4)
Two numbers multiply to −15 and add to 2. What are they? (expected answer: 5 and −3)
notes.watch: Sign slips are the main error: (x + 4)(x − 3) versus (x − 4)(x + 3). Have the student multiply back and look at the middle term.

slides.title: Three Kinds of Factoring
slides.board:
Factor each expression.

(a) 6x2 − 9x    (b) x2 + 2x − 15    (c) x2 − 49
steps: (b) Multiply to −15, add to 2. Pairs: 1 and −15 (−14), −1 and 15 (14), 3 and −5 (−2), −3 and 5 (2) ✓
(c) x2 and 49 = 72 are perfect squares with a minus between → (x + 7)(x − 7)

notes.say: Three different patterns, one routine. Ask in order: Is there a GCF? Is it a trinomial? Is it a difference of squares? In part (b), notice that I list every pair and its sum instead of guessing. That list takes thirty seconds and never misses.
ask: In part (b), why do the two numbers have opposite signs? (expected answer: c = −15 is negative)
notes.watch: If the student writes (x − 5)(x + 3) for part (b), multiply it back: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 15. The middle sign is wrong, so the signs must switch.

slides.title: Factor Completely
slides.board:
(a) Factor completely: 2x2 − 32

(b) Factor completely: 3x2 − 12x − 36
steps: (a) x2 − 16 is a difference of squares: 2(x + 4)(x − 4)
Check (b): (x − 6)(x + 2) = x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 12, and 3 times that is 3x<sup>2</sup> − 12x − 36.

notes.say: “Factor completely” means keep going until nothing else factors. The GCF first makes the numbers smaller and reveals the pattern that was hiding. Without pulling out the 2 in part (a), 2x<sup>2</sup> − 32 does not look like a difference of squares at all.
ask: Is 2(x<sup>2</sup> − 16) factored completely? (expected answer: no; x<sup>2</sup> − 16 still factors)
notes.watch: Students skip the GCF in part (b) and get stuck looking for numbers that multiply to −36 with a leading 3. Send them back to step 1.

slides.title: Your Turn: Factoring
slides.board:
Four minutes. Factor completely, then check one answer by multiplying.

  1. 5x2 + 15x
  2. x2 − 9x + 20
  3. x2 + x − 12
  4. 4x2 − 36

notes.say: Your turn: four minutes. Run the routine on each one: GCF, trinomial, difference of squares. Then pick one answer and multiply it back to prove it.
ask: Read me your answers. (expected answer: 5x(x + 3); (x − 4)(x − 5); (x + 4)(x − 3); 4(x + 3)(x − 3))
notes.answer: (1) GCF 5x: 5x(x + 3)   (2) multiply to 20, add to −9: −4 and −5, so (x − 4)(x − 5)   (3) multiply to −12, add to 1: 4 and −3, so (x + 4)(x − 3)   (4) 4(x<sup>2</sup> − 9) = 4(x + 3)(x − 3)
notes.watch: 4(x<sup>2</sup> − 9) on number 4 is not complete. (x − 4)(x + 3) on number 3 has the signs switched (it multiplies to x<sup>2</sup> − x − 12).

slides.title: GED-Style Question: Area Expression
slides.board:
A square photo with sides x inches long is in a square frame. The frame forms a border 3 inches wide on every side. Which expression is the area of the border only, in square inches?

A. 36    B. 6x + 9    C. 2x2 + 12x + 36    D. 12x + 36

steps: The outer square has side x + 3 + 3 = x + 6. Border area = outer area − photo area = (x + 6)<sup>2</sup> − x<sup>2</sup>.
Eliminate A (36): it comes from squaring (x + 6) as x2 + 36, which drops the middle term 12x.
Eliminate B (6x + 9): it adds the border to only one side, using x + 3 as the outer side.
Eliminate C (2x2 + 12x + 36): it adds the photo area instead of subtracting it.
D (12x + 36) is correct: (x + 6)2 = x2 + 12x + 36; minus x2 leaves 12x + 36. Check x = 10: 162 − 102 = 256 − 100 = 156, and 12(10) + 36 = 156.

notes.say: This is a GED word problem that uses three of today’s skills at once: writing an expression, squaring a binomial, and subtracting polynomials. Sketch it first. The border goes on both sides, so the outer side grows by 6, not 3. Then use “big minus small.”
ask: What is the side length of the outer square? (expected answer: x + 6)
Which choice did you pick? (expected answer: D, 12x + 36)
notes.watch: If the student picked B, point at the figure and count the 3-inch strips across the top: one on the left and one on the right. If A, revisit the binomial-square trap from slide 17.

slides.title: GED Strategy: Plug In a Number
slides.board:
1. For “which expression is equivalent”: choose a simple value such as x = 2 or x = 3 (avoid 0 and 1).
  2. Evaluate the original expression.
  3. Evaluate each choice. Keep the one that matches.
  4. If two choices tie, try a second number.

For factoring, multiply back to check. The formula sheet does not list these rules.

notes.say: When the algebra gets messy, numbers rescue you. Equivalent expressions give the same value for every x, so picking one number and testing each choice catches sign errors and dropped terms. Avoid 0 and 1, because they hide mistakes: x squared and x are both 1 when x is 1. On the calculator section, the TI-30XS makes this fast; on Part 1, use small whole numbers you can do in your head.
ask: Test 4(x + 3) and 4x + 3 with x = 2. Are they equivalent? (expected answer: no; 20 and 11)
notes.watch: Students pick x = 1 and find two choices that match. Show them (x + 1)<sup>2</sup> and x<sup>2</sup> + 3 at x = 1: both equal 4, but they are not equivalent (at x = 2 they are 9 and 7).

screens.title: What You Will Learn
screens.html:
This week you start the heart of algebra: working with letters that stand for numbers. About half of the GED math test is algebra, and the skills in this lesson show up in almost every algebra question. Work one screen at a time. Most screens teach one idea, show a worked example, and end with a check you answer before you move on. Keep paper and a pencil next to you and write every step.

By the end, you will be able to:

  • Translate word phrases into expressions and write cost and perimeter formulas.
  • Evaluate expressions for given values, including negative numbers and exponents.
  • Simplify expressions by combining like terms and using the distributive property.
  • Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
  • Factor using the greatest common factor, trinomial factoring, and the difference of squares.

When a check asks you to type an expression, type it on one line, such as 5x − 7 (use the minus key for negative signs). Any correct order of the terms is accepted, so −7 + 5x also counts, but combine all like terms first.

screens.title: Writing Expressions from Words
screens.html:
A variable is a letter, such as x or n, that stands for a number. An algebraic expression combines numbers, variables, and operations, like 3n + 8. It has no equal sign.

OperationKey wordsExample
Addsum, more than, increased by, plus8 more than n: n + 8
Subtractdifference, less than, decreased by5 less than n: n − 5
Multiplyproduct, times, twice, oftwice n: 2n
Dividequotient, per, divided by, split equallyn split among 4: n/4

Careful: “5 less than n” means start with n and take away 5: n − 5, not 5 − n. Test with a number: 5 less than 20 is 15, and 20 − 5 = 15.

Use parentheses when words group an operation: “twice the sum of n and 3” is 2(n + 3), but “the sum of twice n and 3” is 2n + 3.

example.prompt: Write an expression for “8 more than three times a number n.”
steps: “8 more than” that means add 8 to it.

check.prompt:
Which expression represents the phrase below?

4 less than the product of 7 and a number n
why: You kept the words in reading order. “4 less than” something means start with that something and take 4 away: 7n − 4.
You subtracted 4 from n before multiplying. The product of 7 and n comes first, then 4 is taken away from the whole product.
You treated “product” as a sum. A product means multiply: the product of 7 and n is 7n.
check.hint: “The product of 7 and n” is one quantity. Then “4 less than” that quantity means subtract 4 from it.
check.explain:
“The product of 7 and a number n” is 7n.

“4 less than” 7n means start with 7n and subtract 4: 7n − 4.

Test with n = 10: the product is 70, and 4 less than 70 is 66. 7(10) − 4 = 66. The tempting choice 4 − 7n gives −66, so the order is backward.

screens.title: Writing Formulas: Cost and Perimeter
screens.html:
Many real-life costs follow one pattern:

Cost = flat fee + rate × amount

The flat fee is paid once, no matter how much you use. The rate is charged for each unit (each mile, hour, pound, or month), so it is multiplied by the variable.

Perimeter is the distance around a shape: add all the side lengths. For a rectangle, P = 2l + 2w. If the sides are expressions, add the expressions and combine like terms.

To use a formula, put the number in for the variable and follow the order of operations: multiply the rate by the amount first, then add the fee.

example.prompt: A taxi charges $3.50 plus $2.25 per mile. Write an expression for the cost of a ride of d miles, then find the cost of a 12-mile ride.
steps: Flat fee: 3.50. Rate times miles: 2.25d. Expression: 3.50 + 2.25d.

check.prompt:
A delivery service charges a flat fee of $12 plus $0.80 per pound. The cost is 12 + 0.80p for a package of p pounds.

What is the cost, in dollars, of a 15-pound package?

mistakes.why: You added 12 + 0.80 first and multiplied by 15, which charges the flat fee for every pound. Multiply 0.80 × 15 first, then add the $12 once.
You found only the per-pound charge, 0.80 × 15 = 12. Add the flat fee of $12 too.
You added the fee and the rate (12 + 0.80) but did not multiply the rate by 15 pounds.

check.hint: Substitute 15 for p. Multiply before you add.
check.explain:
Substitute p = 15: 12 + 0.80(15)

Multiply first: 0.80 × 15 = 12

Add the flat fee: 12 + 12 = $24

The tempting wrong answer, $192, comes from adding before multiplying, which charges the $12 fee 15 times.

screens.title: Evaluating Expressions
screens.html:
To evaluate an expression means to find its value. Two steps:

  1. Substitute: replace each variable with its number, written in parentheses.
  2. Compute with the order of operations: grouping, exponents, multiply and divide (left to right), add and subtract (left to right).

A number written right next to a variable means multiply: 3a means 3 × a, and 5xy means 5 × x × y.

Key idea: An exponent applies only to what it touches. In 3x2, only x is squared. If x = 4, then 3x2 = 3(16) = 48, not (12)2 = 144.

mistakes.why: You multiplied 3 × 4 = 12 first and then squared to get 144. The exponent applies only to x: x<sup>2</sup> = 16, then 3(16) = 48.
You doubled x instead of squaring it: 3(4 × 2) = 24. Squaring means 4 × 4 = 16.
You did not square x: 3(4) + 2(5) = 12 + 10. The exponent means x × x = 16.

check.hint: Square x first, then multiply by 3. Then find 2y and add.
check.explain:
Substitute: 3(4)2 + 2(5)

Exponent: (4)2 = 16, so 3(16) = 48

Multiply: 2(5) = 10

Add: 48 + 10 = 58

A common wrong answer is 154, from squaring 3 × 4 instead of squaring only x.

screens.title: Evaluating with Negative Numbers
screens.html:
Negative values are where most evaluating mistakes happen. Parentheses protect you.

If x = −3Write it asValue
x2(−3)2 = (−3)(−3)9
−x2−(−3)2 = −(9)−9
4x4(−3)−12
10 − x10 − (−3) = 10 + 313

Without parentheses, −32 means the negative of 32, which is −9. That is why you must write (−3)2 when x = −3.

Remember from Week 1: subtracting a negative number means adding.

mistakes.why: You treated (−4)<sup>2</sup> as −16. A negative number times itself is positive: (−4)(−4) = 16, so 2(16) = 32.
You found 2(16) = 32 correctly but added 12 instead of adding −12. 3(−4) = −12, so 32 + (−12) = 20.
You squared to −16 and also dropped the sign on 3x: −32 + 12 = −20. (−4)<sup>2</sup> = 16 and 3(−4) = −12.

check.hint: Write (−4) in parentheses everywhere x appears. Square first.
check.explain:
Substitute: 2(−4)2 + 3(−4)

Exponent: (−4)2 = 16, so 2(16) = 32

Multiply: 3(−4) = −12

Add: 32 + (−12) = 20

The tempting wrong answer, −44, comes from writing (−4)2 as −16.

screens.title: Terms, Coefficients, and Like Terms
screens.html:
Terms are the parts of an expression separated by + and − signs. The sign in front of a term belongs to it. In 5x2 − 3x + 7, the terms are 5x2, −3x, and 7.

The coefficient is the number multiplied by the variable (in −3x it is −3; in y it is 1). A term with no variable is a constant.

Like terms have exactly the same variable part, including exponents. 4x and −9x are like terms; 3x and 3x2 are not; 2xy and 5yx are.

To combine like terms, add or subtract the coefficients and keep the variable part: 7x − 2x = 5x. Unlike terms stay separate: 3x + 2 cannot be simplified.

steps: Group like terms, keeping each sign: (7x − 2x) + (3y − 4y) + 5

mistakes.why: You treated −4 − 9 as −4 + 9. Both constants are negative: −4 − 9 = −13.
You subtracted 2a from 6a. The sign in front of 2a is +, so 6a + 2a = 8a.
You combined the a terms with the constants. 8a and −13 are unlike terms, so they stay separate.

check.hint: Group the a terms together and the constants together. Keep each sign with its term.
check.explain:
a terms: 6a + 2a = 8a

Constants: −4 − 9 = −13

Answer: 8a − 13

8a and −13 are unlike terms, so the expression cannot be simplified further.

screens.title: The Distributive Property
screens.html:
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply the outside number by every term inside the parentheses, including its sign.

  • 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12
  • −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10 (a negative times a negative is positive)
  • x(x + 6) = x2 + 6x

Tip: Draw an arrow from the outside number to each term inside. Count the arrows: two terms inside means two products.

After distributing, combine any like terms.

check.prompt:
Use the distributive property to rewrite −4(3x − 5).

Type your answer like 2x + 7.

mistakes.why: You multiplied −4 × (−5) and got −20. A negative times a negative is positive: +20.
You distributed −4 only to 3x. The −4 multiplies the −5 too: −4 × (−5) = +20.
You distributed 4 instead of −4. The negative sign belongs to the 4, so −4 × 3x = −12x and −4 × (−5) = +20.

check.hint: Multiply −4 by 3x, then multiply −4 by −5. Watch the signs.
check.explain:
−4 × 3x = −12x

−4 × (−5) = +20

Answer: −12x + 20

The most common mistake is −12x − 20, which forgets that a negative times a negative is positive.

screens.title: Distribute, Then Combine
screens.html:
Many GED simplifying questions need both moves: first distribute, then combine like terms.

A minus sign in front of parentheses means multiply by −1. It flips the sign of every term inside: −(x + 4) = −x − 4 and −(x − 7) = −x + 7.

Do not let a number in front of the expression “grab” the parentheses. In 6 − 2(3x − 4), the 6 is not multiplied. The −2 is distributed, and then you combine: 6 − 6x + 8 = −6x + 14.

Check any simplification by plugging in a small number such as x = 1 or x = 2 into the original and your answer. They should match.

mistakes.why: You flipped the sign of x but not of 4. The minus in front of (x + 4) flips both terms: −x − 4.
You distributed the 3 only to 2x. It multiplies −1 too: 3(2x − 1) = 6x − 3.
You added x instead of subtracting it. The minus sign in front of the parentheses makes it −x.

check.hint: Distribute the 3. Then treat the minus sign in front of (x + 4) as −1 and flip both signs.
check.explain:
Distribute: 3(2x − 1) = 6x − 3, and −(x + 4) = −x − 4

Rewrite: 6x − 3 − x − 4

Combine: 6x − x = 5x, and −3 − 4 = −7

Answer: 5x − 7

Check with x = 2: 3(3) − 6 = 3, and 5(2) − 7 = 3. If you got 5x + 1, the minus sign flipped only the first term.

screens.title: Polynomials and Standard Form
screens.html:
A polynomial is one term or a sum of terms in which the variables have whole-number exponents, such as 4x2 + 3x − 1.

NameNumber of termsExample
Monomial15x2
Binomial2x + 4
Trinomial3x2 + 3x − 2

Standard form lists the terms from the highest exponent to the lowest, with the constant last. Each term keeps its own sign when you move it.

The degree is the highest exponent. x2 + 3x − 2 has degree 2.

example.prompt: Write 5 + 3x<sup>2</sup> − x in standard form and name it.
steps: The x<sup>2</sup> term goes first, then the x term (with its minus sign), then the constant.

check.prompt:
Complete each statement.

The polynomial 4x3 − 7x + 2 is a {{0}}.

In standard form, 6 − 2x + x2 is written as {{1}}.

why: A monomial has only one term. 4x<sup>3</sup> − 7x + 2 has three terms: 4x<sup>3</sup>, −7x, and 2.
A binomial has two terms. Count the terms separated by + and − signs: 4x<sup>3</sup>, −7x, and 2 make three.
This is the original order. Standard form puts the highest exponent first, so x² leads.
You moved −2x but dropped its minus sign. Each term keeps its own sign when it moves.
This puts the x term first. Standard form goes from the highest exponent (x²) to the lowest.

check.hint: Count the terms. For standard form, order the terms from highest exponent to lowest and keep each sign.
check.explain:
4x3 − 7x + 2 has three terms, so it is a trinomial.

In 6 − 2x + x2, the highest exponent is 2, so x2 comes first, then −2x, then 6: x2 − 2x + 6.

The most common slip is x2 + 2x + 6, which loses the minus sign that belongs to 2x.

screens.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
screens.html:
• Add: remove the parentheses and combine like terms.
  • Subtract: change the sign of every term in the second polynomial, then combine like terms.

The minus sign in front of the second polynomial is a −1 that is distributed to every term. Flipping only the first sign is the most common mistake on this topic. Always write a “flip line” before combining.

It can help to sort the terms into columns: x2 terms, x terms, and constants.

steps: Flip every sign in the second polynomial: 4x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 1 − x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 6
x<sup>2</sup> terms: 4x<sup>2</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> = 3x<sup>2</sup>. x terms: 3x + 2x = 5x. Constants: −1 − 6 = −7

check.prompt:
Subtract: (6x2 + x − 4) − (2x2 − 5x − 9)

The result can be written as 4x2 + bx + c. What is the value of b, the coefficient of x?

mistakes.why: You combined x and −5x without flipping the sign of −5x. Subtracting −5x means adding 5x: x + 5x = 6x.

check.hint: Write the flip line first: every term in the second polynomial changes sign.
check.explain:
Flip every sign in the second polynomial: 6x2 + x − 4 − 2x2 + 5x + 9

x2 terms: 6x2 − 2x2 = 4x2. x terms: x + 5x = 6x. Constants: −4 + 9 = 5

Result: 4x2 + 6x + 5, so b = 6.

If you got −4, you did not flip the sign of −5x.

screens.title: Multiplying Monomials and Polynomials
screens.html:
To multiply terms, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents of the same variable. A variable with no written exponent has exponent 1.

  • x × x = x2 (not 2x)
  • 4x × 5x = 20x2
  • 3x × 2x2 = 6x3

To multiply a monomial by a polynomial, distribute: multiply the monomial by every term.

Adding terms and multiplying terms follow different rules: x + x = 2x, but x × x = x2.

why: You multiplied by 2 but not by x. Each product also gets an extra factor of x: 2x × 3x<sup>2</sup> = 6x<sup>3</sup>, 2x × (−5x) = −10x<sup>2</sup>, and 2x × 1 = 2x.
You multiplied 2x by only the first term. Distribute 2x to all three terms: −5x and 1 must be multiplied too.
You added the coefficients (2 + 3, 2 − 5, 2 + 1) instead of multiplying them. 2 × 3 = 6, 2 × (−5) = −10, and 2 × 1 = 2.
check.hint: Multiply 2x by each of the three terms. Multiply coefficients; add exponents.
check.explain:
2x × 3x2 = 6x3

2x × (−5x) = −10x2

2x × 1 = 2x

Answer: 6x3 − 10x2 + 2x

The choice 6x2 − 10x + 2 multiplies by 2 only and forgets the x in 2x.

screens.title: Multiplying Two Binomials
screens.html:
To multiply two binomials, every term in the first multiplies every term in the second: four products. FOIL helps you remember them:

  • First terms
  • Outer terms
  • Inner terms
  • Last terms

Then combine the like terms (usually the two middle products).

A box works the same way: write one binomial across the top and the other down the side, fill in the four products, and add.

×x+3
xx23x
−7−7x−21

steps: First: x × x = x<sup>2</sup>. Outer: x × (−7) = −7x. Inner: 3 × x = 3x. Last: 3 × (−7) = −21

check.prompt:
(x + 6)(x − 2) = x2 + bx − 12

What is the value of b?

mistakes.why: You added 6 and 2 and ignored the minus sign. The outer product is x × (−2) = −2x, and the inner is 6x: −2x + 6x = 4x.
You reversed the signs of the middle products. x × (−2) = −2x and 6 × x = +6x, so the sum is +4x.
You gave both middle products a negative sign. Only the outer product is negative: −2x + 6x = 4x.

check.hint: Find the outer product and the inner product, then add them.
check.explain:
First: x2. Outer: x × (−2) = −2x. Inner: 6 × x = 6x. Last: 6 × (−2) = −12

Middle terms: −2x + 6x = 4x, so the product is x2 + 4x − 12 and b = 4.

If you got 8, you added 6 and 2 without the sign of −2.

screens.title: Special Products
screens.html:
Two patterns appear often on the GED.

Square of a binomial. (a + b)2 means (a + b)(a + b). It has a middle term:

  • (x + 5)2 = x2 + 5x + 5x + 25 = x2 + 10x + 25
  • (x − 3)2 = x2 − 3x − 3x + 9 = x2 − 6x + 9

(x + 5)2 is not x2 + 25. Test x = 1: (1 + 5)2 = 36, but 1 + 25 = 26.

Sum times difference. (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2. The middle terms cancel:

  • (x − 6)(x + 6) = x2 + 6x − 6x − 36 = x2 − 36

why: You squared each term and kept the minus sign. (x − 4)<sup>2</sup> means (x − 4)(x − 4), which has a middle term of −8x and a last term of (−4)(−4) = +16.
You found the middle term but made the last product negative. (−4)(−4) = +16.
You included only one middle product. Both the outer and inner products are −4x, and they add to −8x.
check.hint: Write (x − 4)<sup>2</sup> as (x − 4)(x − 4) and find all four products.
check.explain:
(x − 4)(x − 4): First x2. Outer −4x. Inner −4x. Last (−4)(−4) = +16.

Combine: x2 − 8x + 16.

Check x = 5: (5 − 4)2 = 1, and 25 − 40 + 16 = 1. The choice x2 − 16 gives 9 at x = 5, so it is not equivalent.

screens.title: Factoring Out the Greatest Common Factor
screens.html:
Factoring is multiplying in reverse: you write an expression as a product. You can always check a factoring by multiplying it back out.

Step 1 of every factoring problem: look for the greatest common factor (GCF), the largest number and the highest power of each variable that divide every term.

  1. Find the GCF of the coefficients.
  2. Take the lowest power of each variable that appears in every term.
  3. Write the GCF in front and divide each term by it.

Make sure nothing common is left inside: 3x2(4x − 6) still has a common factor of 2.

steps: GCF of 12 and 18 is 6. Lowest power of x is x<sup>2</sup>. GCF = 6x<sup>2</sup>

check.prompt:
Fill in the greatest common factor:

10x2 + 25x = ___(2x + 5)

Type only the factor that goes in front.

mistakes.why: You found the number part only. Both terms also contain x, so the GCF is 5x. Check: 5(2x + 5) = 10x + 25, not 10x<sup>2</sup> + 25x.
You found the variable part only. 10 and 25 also share the factor 5, so the GCF is 5x.
You used the highest power of x. The GCF uses the lowest power that appears in every term; 25x has only x. Check: 5x<sup>2</sup>(2x + 5) = 10x<sup>3</sup> + 25x<sup>2</sup>.

check.hint: What is the largest number that divides 10 and 25? What power of x appears in both terms?
check.explain:
GCF of 10 and 25: 5. Both terms contain x, and the lowest power is x. GCF = 5x.

10x2 ÷ 5x = 2x and 25x ÷ 5x = 5, so 10x2 + 25x = 5x(2x + 5).

Check by distributing: 5x(2x) + 5x(5) = 10x2 + 25x.

screens.title: Factoring Trinomials
screens.html:
To factor a trinomial of the form x2 + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. Then write (x + first number)(x + second number).

SignsThe two numbers
c positive, b positiveboth positive
c positive, b negativeboth negative
c negativeone positive, one negative

List the factor pairs of c and add each pair until you find b. Then multiply back to check.

steps: c = −12 is negative, so the numbers have opposite signs. They must add to b = −1.
Pairs: 1 and −12 (−11), 2 and −6 (−4), 3 and −4 (−1). The pair 3 and −4 works.

check.prompt:
The trinomial x2 − 2x − 24 factors as (x + 4)(x + k).

What is the value of k?

mistakes.why: You found the right size but the wrong sign. (x + 4)(x + 6) = x<sup>2</sup> + 10x + 24. The numbers must multiply to −24, so one of them is negative: 4 × (−6) = −24 and 4 + (−6) = −2.
You made 4 + k equal to c = −24. The two numbers must multiply to −24 and add to −2: 4 × (−6) = −24 and 4 + (−6) = −2.

check.hint: The two numbers are 4 and k. They must multiply to −24 and add to −2.
check.explain:
The two numbers multiply to −24 and add to −2.

4 × k = −24 gives k = −6. Check the sum: 4 + (−6) = −2. It works.

So x2 − 2x − 24 = (x + 4)(x − 6), and k = −6.

Check: x2 − 6x + 4x − 24 = x2 − 2x − 24.

screens.title: Difference of Squares and Factoring Completely
screens.html:
A difference of squares is one perfect square minus another. It factors as:

a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b)

Examples: x2 − 49 = (x + 7)(x − 7) and x2 − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1). A sum of squares, such as x2 + 49, does not factor this way.

Factor completely means keep going until no factor can be factored again. Always take out the GCF first; it often uncovers a difference of squares or a simpler trinomial.

steps: x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = x<sup>2</sup> − 3<sup>2</sup>, a difference of squares: (x + 3)(x − 3)

check.prompt:
When 2x2 − 72 is factored completely, it can be written as 2(x + a)(x − a), where a is a positive number.

What is the value of a?

mistakes.why: You stopped at 2(x<sup>2</sup> − 36). The number 36 is 6<sup>2</sup>, so x<sup>2</sup> − 36 = (x + 6)(x − 6), and a = 6.
You took the square root of 72 without factoring out the GCF. First write 2x<sup>2</sup> − 72 = 2(x<sup>2</sup> − 36); then 36 = 6<sup>2</sup>.

check.hint: Factor out the GCF first. Then look for a difference of squares.
check.explain:
GCF: 2x2 − 72 = 2(x2 − 36)

Difference of squares: x2 − 36 = (x + 6)(x − 6)

So 2x2 − 72 = 2(x + 6)(x − 6), and a = 6.

If you got 36, you stopped one step early: 36 is 62.

screens.title: Checking with a Number
screens.html:
Two expressions are equivalent if they give the same value for every value of the variable. The GED often asks, “Which expression is equivalent to…?”

You can check any answer by plugging in a number:

  1. Pick a simple value, such as x = 2 or x = 3. Avoid 0 and 1; they can make different expressions look the same.
  2. Evaluate the original expression.
  3. Evaluate your answer (or each choice). Equivalent expressions match.

This also checks factoring: (x + 3)(x − 4) and x2 − x − 12 should give the same value at x = 2.

example.answer: 3(x − 2) + x is equivalent to 4x − 6, not to 4x − 2.

why: You multiplied −3 × (−1) and got −3. A negative times a negative is positive, so the last term is +3, and 10 + 3 = 13.
You added 2x and 3x. The −3 is distributed, so the x terms are 2x − 3x = −x.
You distributed −3 only to x and kept −1 as it was. −3 × (−1) = +3, so the constants are 10 + 3 = 13.
check.hint: Distribute 2 and −3, then combine. Check with x = 2.
check.explain:
Distribute: 2x + 10 − 3x + 3

Combine: 2x − 3x = −x, and 10 + 3 = 13

Answer: −x + 13

Check x = 2: 2(7) − 3(1) = 11, and −2 + 13 = 11. The choice −x + 7 gives 5 at x = 2, so it is not equivalent.

screens.title: Summary
screens.html:
• “Less than” flips the order: 5 less than n is n − 5. Use parentheses for grouped words: twice the sum of n and 3 is 2(n + 3).
  • Cost = flat fee + rate × amount. Perimeter = sum of all sides.
  • Evaluate: substitute in parentheses, then use the order of operations. (−3)2 = 9, but −32 = −9.
  • Like terms have the same variable part. Combine coefficients only.
  • Distribute to every term, signs included. A minus in front of parentheses flips every sign.
  • Subtract polynomials: flip every sign in the second, then combine. Multiply: every term times every term; add exponents.
  • (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2, not a2 + b2. (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2.
  • Factor: GCF first; then a trinomial (multiply to c, add to b) or a difference of squares. Multiply back to check.
  • Not sure? Plug in x = 2 and compare.

Next: Practice Set A. If you score under 80%, practice the same skills again with Set B. Then take the Exit Check.

items.prompt:
Which expression represents the phrase below?

5 less than twice a number n
why: You kept the words in reading order. “5 less than” twice a number means start with 2n and take 5 away: 2n − 5. Test n = 10: 5 less than 20 is 15, but 5 − 20 = −15.
You subtracted 5 from n before doubling. “Twice a number” is found first, and then 5 is taken away from 2n.
You added 5. “Less than” means subtract.
items.hint: “Twice a number” is 2n. “5 less than” something means you start with that something and take 5 away.
items.explain:
“Twice a number n” is 2n.

“5 less than” 2n means start with 2n and subtract 5: 2n − 5.

Test with n = 10: twice 10 is 20, and 5 less than 20 is 15. 2(10) − 5 = 15. Correct.

5 − 2n reverses the order (it gives −15 for n = 10). 2(n − 5) subtracts 5 before doubling, which gives 10. 2n + 5 adds instead of subtracting.

items.prompt:
What is the value of the expression below when x = −2?

3x2 − 4x + 7

mistakes.why: You treated (−2)<sup>2</sup> as −4, so 3(−4) = −12. A negative number squared is positive: (−2)(−2) = 4, so 3(4) = 12.
You subtracted 8 instead of adding it. −4(−2) = +8, so subtracting 4x adds 8: 12 + 8 + 7 = 27.
You squared to −4 and also subtracted 8: −12 − 8 + 7. (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4, and −4(−2) = +8.

items.hint: Replace x with (−2), in parentheses. Square first, then multiply, then add and subtract.
items.explain:
Substitute with parentheses: 3(−2)2 − 4(−2) + 7

Exponent: (−2)2 = 4, so 3(4) = 12

Multiply: 4(−2) = −8, and subtracting −8 means adding 8

12 + 8 + 7 = 27

A common mistake is treating (−2)2 as −4, which gives −12 + 8 + 7 = 3. Another is subtracting 8 instead of adding it, which gives 12 − 8 + 7 = 11.

items.prompt:
A landscaping company charges a $45 trip fee plus $28 per hour of work. The cost C, in dollars, for h hours is C = 45 + 28h.

What is the cost of a job that takes 2.5 hours?

mistakes.why: You added 45 + 28 first and multiplied by 2.5, which charges the trip fee for every hour. Multiply 28 × 2.5 first, then add the $45 once.
You found only the hourly charge, 28 × 2.5 = 70. Add the $45 trip fee.
You found the cost of one hour, 45 + 28. The job takes 2.5 hours, so multiply 28 by 2.5.

items.hint: Substitute 2.5 for h. Multiply before you add.
items.explain:
Substitute h = 2.5: C = 45 + 28(2.5)

Multiply first: 28 × 2.5 = 70

Add the trip fee: 45 + 70 = $115

The tempting wrong answer, $182.50, comes from adding before multiplying, which charges the trip fee 2.5 times.

items.prompt:
Simplify: 8x + 5 − 3x − 9 + x

Type your answer like 2x + 7.

mistakes.why: You subtracted the last x. Its sign is +, so the x terms are 8x − 3x + x = 6x.
You added 9 instead of subtracting it. The constants are 5 − 9 = −4.
You combined the x terms with the constants. 6x and −4 are unlike terms, so they stay separate.

items.hint: Collect the x terms (8x, −3x, +x) and the constants (5, −9). Keep each sign with its term.
items.explain:
x terms: 8x − 3x + x = 6x (the lone x has coefficient 1)

Constants: 5 − 9 = −4

Answer: 6x − 4

A common slip is 4x − 4, which forgets that x means +1x.

items.prompt:
A student simplifies the expression −3(2x − 5) + 4x. Choose the correct expression for each step.

Step 1 (distribute): −3(2x − 5) + 4x = {{0}} + 4x

Step 2 (combine like terms): = {{1}}

why: You made −3 × (−5) negative. A negative times a negative is positive: +15.
You dropped the negative on the 3. −3 × 2x = −6x, and −3 × (−5) = +15.
You distributed −3 only to 2x and kept −5 as it was. The −3 multiplies both terms.
You added 6x and 4x and ignored the negative on −6x. −6x + 4x = −2x.
You combined the x terms correctly but changed +15 to −15. The constant from Step 1 is +15.
You lost the sign: −6x + 4x is −2x, because the negative term is larger.

items.hint: Multiply −3 by both terms inside the parentheses. A negative times a negative is positive.
items.explain:
Step 1: Distribute −3 to both terms:

−3 × 2x = −6x and −3 × (−5) = +15

So the expression becomes −6x + 15 + 4x.

Step 2: Combine the x terms: −6x + 4x = −2x. The constant 15 stays.

Answer: −2x + 15

−6x − 15 is a sign error: (−3)(−5) is positive. −6x − 5 distributes to only the first term. 10x + 15 comes from adding 6 and 4 while ignoring the negative sign on 6x.

items.prompt:
A triangle has sides of length (2x + 3) cm, (x + 5) cm, and (4x − 1) cm. Write a simplified expression for the perimeter of the triangle.

Type your answer like 3x + 2.

mistakes.why: You added 1 instead of subtracting it. The constants are 3 + 5 − 1 = 7.
You skipped the x in (x + 5). It has a coefficient of 1, so the x terms are 2x + x + 4x = 7x.
You combined the x terms with the constants. 7x and 7 are unlike terms, so the perimeter is 7x + 7.

items.hint: Perimeter means add all three sides. Then combine the x terms and the constants separately.
items.explain:
Add the sides: (2x + 3) + (x + 5) + (4x − 1)

x terms: 2x + x + 4x = 7x

Constants: 3 + 5 − 1 = 7

Perimeter: 7x + 7 cm

Check with x = 2: the sides are 7, 7, and 7, for a total of 21, and 7(2) + 7 = 21.

items.prompt:
Which expression is equivalent to the expression below?

(5x2 − 3x + 8) − (2x2 + 4x − 6)
why: You flipped the sign of 2x<sup>2</sup> but not of 4x and −6. The minus sign changes every term: −2x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 6.
You flipped the x term but forgot that subtracting −6 means adding 6. The constants are 8 + 6 = 14.
You added the polynomials instead of subtracting: 5x<sup>2</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> = 7x<sup>2</sup>. Change every sign in the second polynomial first.
items.hint: The minus sign in front of the second set of parentheses changes the sign of every term inside it.
items.explain:
Change the sign of every term in the second polynomial:

5x2 − 3x + 8 − 2x2 − 4x + 6

x2 terms: 5x2 − 2x2 = 3x2

x terms: −3x − 4x = −7x

Constants: 8 + 6 = 14

Answer: 3x2 − 7x + 14

3x2 + x + 2 flips only the first sign. 3x2 − 7x + 2 forgets that subtracting −6 means adding 6. 7x2 + x + 2 adds the two polynomials instead of subtracting.

items.prompt: Drag each expression into the correct bin: equivalent to 4(x + 3) or not equivalent to 4(x + 3).
items.why: The most common mistake is putting 4x + 3 in the equivalent bin. Distributing 4 to only the x gives 4x + 3, but 4 multiplies the 3 too: 4(x + 3) = 4x + 12. Test x = 2: 4(5) = 20, while 4(2) + 3 = 11.
items.hint: Simplify each expression, then compare it with 4(x + 3) = 4x + 12. You can also test x = 2: 4(2 + 3) = 20.
items.explain:
First simplify 4(x + 3) = 4x + 12.

4x + 12: the same. Equivalent.

2(2x + 6) = 4x + 12. Equivalent.

3x + 9 + x + 3 = (3x + x) + (9 + 3) = 4x + 12. Equivalent.

4(3 + x) = 12 + 4x = 4x + 12 (order of adding does not matter). Equivalent.

4x + 3 distributes the 4 to only the x. Not equivalent (at x = 2 it equals 11, not 20).

16x combines unlike terms, 4x and 12, into one term. Not equivalent (at x = 2 it equals 32, not 20).

items.prompt:
Which expression is equivalent to the product below?

(3x + 2)(x − 4)
why: You multiplied only the first terms and the last terms. FOIL has four products: the outer (−12x) and inner (2x) products are missing.
You reversed the signs of the middle products. Outer: 3x × (−4) = −12x. Inner: 2 × x = +2x. Together: −10x.
You made the inner product negative. 2 × x = +2x, so −12x + 2x = −10x, not −14x.
items.hint: Use FOIL: First, Outer, Inner, Last. Then combine the two middle terms.
items.explain:
First: 3x × x = 3x2. Outer: 3x × (−4) = −12x. Inner: 2 × x = 2x. Last: 2 × (−4) = −8

Combine: −12x + 2x = −10x

Answer: 3x2 − 10x − 8

The choice 3x2 − 8 skips the outer and inner products; that is the most common shortcut error.

items.prompt:
Evaluate the expression when a = −2 and b = 5.

a2 − 3ab + 2b

mistakes.why: You made −3ab negative. −3(−2)(5) = +30, because there are two negative factors.
You treated (−2)<sup>2</sup> as −4. A negative number squared is positive: (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4.
You squared to −4 and also made −3ab negative: −4 − 30 + 10. (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4 and −3(−2)(5) = +30.

items.hint: Write (−2) and (5) in parentheses. Find a<sup>2</sup> first, then the product −3ab, then 2b.
items.explain:
Substitute: (−2)2 − 3(−2)(5) + 2(5)

Exponent: (−2)2 = 4

Multiply: −3(−2)(5) = 30 and 2(5) = 10

Add: 4 + 30 + 10 = 44

The tempting wrong answer, −16, comes from treating −3(−2)(5) as −30.

items.prompt:
The square of a binomial can be written as a trinomial:

(2x − 5)2 = 4x2 + bx + 25

What is the value of b?

mistakes.why: You squared each term: (2x)<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup>. A squared binomial has a middle term. Write (2x − 5)(2x − 5): the outer and inner products are −10x and −10x.
You counted only one middle product. The outer and inner products are both −10x, so b = −20.
You lost the sign. Each middle product is 2x × (−5) = −10x, so the sum is −20x.

items.hint: Write the square as (2x − 5)(2x − 5) and find the outer and inner products.
items.explain:
(2x − 5)(2x − 5): First 4x2. Outer 2x × (−5) = −10x. Inner −5 × 2x = −10x. Last (−5)(−5) = 25

Middle terms: −10x − 10x = −20x, so (2x − 5)2 = 4x2 − 20x + 25 and b = −20.

Check with x = 1: (2 − 5)2 = 9, and 4 − 20 + 25 = 9. The tempting answer 0 comes from squaring term by term.

items.prompt:
When the expression 3x2 − 48 is factored completely, it can be written in the form 3(x + a)(x − a), where a is a positive number.

What is the value of a?

mistakes.why: You stopped at 3(x<sup>2</sup> − 16). 16 is 4<sup>2</sup>, so x<sup>2</sup> − 16 = (x + 4)(x − 4), and a = 4.
You took the square root of 48 without factoring out the GCF. First write 3x<sup>2</sup> − 48 = 3(x<sup>2</sup> − 16).
You used the constant 48 directly. Factor out the GCF 3 first, then take the square root of 16.

items.hint: Factor out the greatest common factor first. Then look for a difference of squares.
items.explain:
Step 1, GCF: both 3x2 and 48 are divisible by 3.

3x2 − 48 = 3(x2 − 16)

Step 2, difference of squares: x2 − 16 = x2 − 42 = (x + 4)(x − 4)

So 3x2 − 48 = 3(x + 4)(x − 4), and a = 4.

Check: 3(x + 4)(x − 4) = 3(x2 − 16) = 3x2 − 48.

A common wrong answer is 16, which comes from stopping at 3(x2 − 16) and forgetting that 16 = 42. Another is about 6.93 (the square root of 48), which comes from skipping the GCF step.

items.prompt:
The expression x2 − 3x − 18 can be written as a product of two binomials. Which binomials are its factors?

Select two answers.
why: x + 6 pairs with x − 3: (x + 6)(x − 3) = x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 18. The middle term is +3x, so the signs are switched.
x − 3 pairs with x + 6, which gives x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 18. You need numbers that add to −3, so the larger number is negative: 3 and −6.
x − 9 pairs with x + 2: (x − 9)(x + 2) = x<sup>2</sup> − 7x − 18. The numbers multiply to −18 but add to −7, not −3.
x + 2 pairs with x − 9, which gives x<sup>2</sup> − 7x − 18. The sum −7 does not match the middle coefficient −3.
items.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to −18 and add to −3.
items.explain:
For x2 + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c = −18 and add to b = −3.

Factor pairs of −18 with opposite signs: 1 and −18 (sum −17), −1 and 18 (sum 17), 2 and −9 (sum −7), −2 and 9 (sum 7), 3 and −6 (sum −3), −3 and 6 (sum 3).

The pair 3 and −6 works, so x2 − 3x − 18 = (x + 3)(x − 6).

Check: x2 − 6x + 3x − 18 = x2 − 3x − 18.

(x + 6)(x − 3) = x2 + 3x − 18, which has the wrong sign on the middle term. (x − 9)(x + 2) = x2 − 7x − 18, which has the wrong middle term.

items.prompt: A rectangular garden is (2x + 3) feet long and (x − 2) feet wide. Which expression represents the area of the garden, in square feet?
why: You multiplied only the first terms and the last terms. FOIL has four products: the outer product −4x and the inner product 3x combine to −x.
You found the perimeter: 2(2x + 3) + 2(x − 2) = 6x + 2. Area of a rectangle is length × width.
You made the outer product positive. 2x × (−2) = −4x, and −4x + 3x = −x.
items.hint: Area of a rectangle = length × width. Multiply the two binomials with FOIL.
items.explain:
Area = (2x + 3)(x − 2)

First: 2x × x = 2x2. Outer: 2x × (−2) = −4x. Inner: 3 × x = 3x. Last: 3 × (−2) = −6

Combine: −4x + 3x = −x. Area: 2x2 − x − 6 square feet

Check with x = 4: the garden is 11 ft by 2 ft, area 22. And 2(16) − 4 − 6 = 22. The choice 6x + 2 is the perimeter, not the area.

items.prompt:
Print Shop A charges an $18 setup fee plus $0.35 per flyer. Print Shop B charges $0.50 per flyer with no setup fee.

For an order of 200 flyers, how many more dollars does Shop B charge than Shop A?

mistakes.why: You found the cost at Shop A: 18 + 0.35(200) = 88. The question asks for the difference: 100 − 88.
You found the cost at Shop B: 0.50(200) = 100. Subtract Shop A’s cost of $88.
You computed Shop A as (18 + 0.35) × 200 = 3,670, which charges the setup fee for every flyer. Shop A costs 18 + 0.35(200) = 88.

items.hint: Write an expression for each shop with f flyers, then substitute 200 into both.
items.explain:
Shop A: 18 + 0.35f. For f = 200: 18 + 0.35(200) = 18 + 70 = $88

Shop B: 0.50f. For f = 200: 0.50(200) = $100

Difference: 100 − 88 = $12 more at Shop B.

Stopping after one shop is the most common error; the question asks how much more.

items.prompt:

the product of 6 and a number n, decreased by 4

Type your answer like 3n + 1.

mistakes.why: You reversed the subtraction. “Decreased by 4” means start with 6n and take 4 away: 6n − 4.
You subtracted 4 from n before multiplying. The product 6n comes first, and then the whole product is decreased by 4.
“Decreased by” means subtract, not add.

items.hint: Find the product first. Then decrease it, which means subtract.
items.explain:
“The product of 6 and a number n” is 6n.

“Decreased by 4” means subtract 4 from it: 6n − 4.

Test n = 10: the product is 60, and 60 decreased by 4 is 56. 6(10) − 4 = 56.

4x2 − 3x + 2

You subtracted 9 instead of adding it. −3(−3) = +9, so 36 + 9 + 2 = 47.
You squared to −9 and also subtracted 9: −36 − 9 + 2. (−3)<sup>2</sup> = 9 and −3(−3) = +9.

items.hint: Replace x with (−3) in parentheses. Square first, then multiply, then add and subtract.
items.explain:
Substitute: 4(−3)2 − 3(−3) + 2

Exponent: (−3)2 = 9, so 4(9) = 36

Multiply: −3(−3) = +9

Add: 36 + 9 + 2 = 47

items.prompt:
A plumber charges a $65 service fee for each visit plus $48 per hour of work. The total cost C for h hours of work is given by the formula C = 65 + 48h.

What is the total cost of a visit with 3.5 hours of work?
why: You added 65 + 48 first and then multiplied by 3.5, which charges the service fee for every hour. Multiply 48 × 3.5 first.
You found only the hourly charge, 48 × 3.5 = 168. Add the $65 service fee once.
You found the cost of one hour, 65 + 48. The visit has 3.5 hours of work, so multiply 48 by 3.5.
items.hint: Substitute 3.5 for h. Multiply 48 by 3.5 before adding the 65.
items.explain:
Substitute h = 3.5: C = 65 + 48(3.5)

Multiply first: 48 × 3.5 = 168

Add the service fee: 65 + 168 = $233.00

$395.50 comes from adding first, (65 + 48) × 3.5, which charges the service fee for every hour. $168.00 leaves out the service fee. $113.00 is 65 + 48, the cost of only one hour.

items.prompt:
Which expression is equivalent to the expression below?

8x + 2y − 3x − 6 − 5y
why: You dropped the negative on the y term. 2y − 5y = −3y, because the subtracted term is larger.
You added 8x and 3x. The sign in front of 3x is minus, so 8x − 3x = 5x.
You added 5y instead of subtracting it. The sign in front of 5y is minus, so 2y − 5y = −3y.
items.hint: Group the x terms, the y terms, and the constants. Keep the sign in front of each term.
items.explain:
Group like terms, keeping each sign with its term:

x terms: 8x − 3x = 5x

y terms: 2y − 5y = −3y

Constant: −6

Answer: 5x − 3y − 6

5x + 3y − 6 drops the negative on the y term (2 − 5 is −3, not 3). 11x − 3y − 6 adds 8x and 3x instead of subtracting. 5x + 7y − 6 adds 5y instead of subtracting it.

Step 1 (distribute): −2(4x − 3) + 5x = {{0}} + 5x

Step 2 (combine like terms): = {{1}}

why: You made −2 × (−3) negative. A negative times a negative is positive: +6.
You dropped the negative on the 2. −2 × 4x = −8x.
You distributed −2 only to 4x and left −3 as it was. The −2 multiplies both terms.

Step 1: −2 × 4x = −8x and −2 × (−3) = +6, so the expression is −8x + 6 + 5x.

items.prompt: A rectangular rug has a length of (3x + 4) feet and a width of (x − 1) feet. Which expression represents the perimeter of the rug, in feet?

figure.alt: A rectangle labeled 3x + 4 feet along its length and x minus 1 feet along its width.
figure.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 170' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='50' y='40' width='190' height='90' fill='#F3E9C9' stroke='#0A1F3D' stroke-width='2'/><text x='145' y='30' text-anchor='middle' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>3x + 4 ft</text><text x='246' y='90' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>x − 1 ft</text></svg>

why: You added the length and width only once, which is half the perimeter. A rectangle has two lengths and two widths.
You wrote 2(x − 1) as 2x + 2. Distribute the sign too: 2 × (−1) = −2, so the constants are 8 − 2 = 6.
You multiplied the length by the width. That gives the area, not the perimeter. Perimeter is the distance around: 2l + 2w.
items.hint: Perimeter of a rectangle: P = 2l + 2w. Distribute the 2 to both terms of each side length.
items.explain:
Use P = 2l + 2w:

P = 2(3x + 4) + 2(x − 1)

Distribute: 6x + 8 + 2x − 2

Combine: 6x + 2x = 8x and 8 − 2 = 6

Perimeter: 8x + 6 feet

4x + 3 adds the length and width only once (that is half the perimeter). 8x + 10 comes from writing 2(x − 1) as 2x + 2. 3x2 + x − 4 is the area, (3x + 4)(x − 1), not the perimeter.

The result can be written as 4x2 + 6x + c. What is the value of c?

mistakes.why: You did not flip the sign of +8, so you computed −5 + 8. Subtracting +8 means −5 − 8 = −13.
You found the right size but the wrong sign. −5 − 8 = −13.

Flip every sign in the second polynomial: 7x2 + 2x − 5 − 3x2 + 4x − 8

x2 terms: 4x2. x terms: 2x + 4x = 6x. Constants: −5 − 8 = −13

Result: 4x2 + 6x − 13, so c = −13.

(2x − 5)(x + 3)

Outer: 2x × 3 = 6x

Inner: −5 × x = −5x

Last: −5 × 3 = −15

Combine the middle terms: 6x − 5x = x

Answer: 2x2 + x − 15

Check x = 2: (4 − 5)(5) = −5, and 8 + 2 − 15 = −5.

items.prompt:
Evaluate the expression when x = 4 and y = −2.

3xy − y2

You dropped the sign of y in the product. 3(4)(−2) = −24, not 24.
You made both parts positive. 3(4)(−2) = −24, and −(−2)<sup>2</sup> = −4, so the total is −28.

Substitute: 3(4)(−2) − (−2)2

Multiply: 3(4)(−2) = −24

Exponent: (−2)2 = 4, so −(−2)2 = −4

Combine: −24 − 4 = −28

items.prompt:
The square of a binomial can be written as a trinomial:

(3x + 4)2 = 9x2 + bx + 16

What is the value of b?

mistakes.why: You squared each term: (3x)<sup>2</sup> + 4<sup>2</sup>. A squared binomial has a middle term. Write (3x + 4)(3x + 4): the outer and inner products are 12x and 12x.
You counted only one middle product. The outer and inner products are both 12x, so b = 24.
You added 3 and 4. The middle products are 3x × 4 = 12x twice, so b = 24.

items.hint: Write the square as (3x + 4)(3x + 4) and find the outer and inner products.
items.explain:
(3x + 4)(3x + 4): First 9x2. Outer 3x × 4 = 12x. Inner 4 × 3x = 12x. Last 16

Middle terms: 12x + 12x = 24x, so (3x + 4)2 = 9x2 + 24x + 16 and b = 24.

Check with x = 1: (3 + 4)2 = 49, and 9 + 24 + 16 = 49. The tempting answer 0 comes from squaring term by term.

items.prompt:
When the expression 6x2 − 54 is factored completely, it can be written in the form 6(x + a)(x − a), where a is a positive number.

What is the value of a?

mistakes.why: You stopped at 6(x<sup>2</sup> − 9). 9 is 3<sup>2</sup>, so x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3), and a = 3.
You took the square root of 54 without factoring out the GCF. First write 6x<sup>2</sup> − 54 = 6(x<sup>2</sup> − 9).
You used the constant 54 directly. Factor out the GCF 6 first, then take the square root of 9.

items.hint: Factor out the greatest common factor first. Then look for a difference of squares.
items.explain:
Step 1, GCF: 6x2 − 54 = 6(x2 − 9)

Step 2, difference of squares: x2 − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3)

So 6x2 − 54 = 6(x + 3)(x − 3), and a = 3.

Check: 6(x2 − 9) = 6x2 − 54. A common wrong answer is 9, from stopping before the difference of squares.

items.prompt:
The expression x2 + 2x − 24 can be written as a product of two binomials. Which binomials are its factors?

Select two answers.
why: x − 6 pairs with x + 4: (x − 6)(x + 4) = x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 24. The middle term is −2x, so the signs are switched.
x + 4 pairs with x − 6, which gives x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 24. You need numbers that add to +2, so the larger number is positive: 6 and −4.
x + 8 pairs with x − 3: (x + 8)(x − 3) = x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 24. The numbers multiply to −24 but add to 5, not 2.
x − 3 pairs with x + 8, which gives x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 24. The sum 5 does not match the middle coefficient 2.
items.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to −24 and add to 2.
items.explain:
Find two numbers that multiply to c = −24 and add to b = 2.

Pairs with opposite signs: 1 and −24 (−23), 2 and −12 (−10), 3 and −8 (−5), 4 and −6 (−2), −4 and 6 (2) ✓

So x2 + 2x − 24 = (x + 6)(x − 4). Check: x2 − 4x + 6x − 24 = x2 + 2x − 24.

(x − 6)(x + 4) is the most tempting wrong pair: it multiplies to −24, but its middle term is −2x.

items.prompt:

Which expression represents the area of the border only, in square inches?

figure.alt: A square photo with side length x inches inside a square frame. The border is 2 inches wide on every side.

why: You added the border to only one side, so the outer side was x + 2. The border is on both sides, so the outer side is x + 4.
You squared (x + 4) as x<sup>2</sup> + 16 and left out the middle term 8x. (x + 4)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 16.
You added the photo area instead of subtracting it. Border area = outer area − photo area.
items.hint: Find the side length of the outer square first (the border is on both sides). Border area = outer area − photo area.
items.explain:
The border adds 2 inches on the left and 2 inches on the right, so the outer square has side x + 2 + 2 = x + 4.

Outer area: (x + 4)2 = (x + 4)(x + 4) = x2 + 4x + 4x + 16 = x2 + 8x + 16

Photo area: x2

Border area: (x2 + 8x + 16) − x2 = 8x + 16

Check with x = 10: outer square 14 × 14 = 196, photo 10 × 10 = 100, border 96. And 8(10) + 16 = 96.

4x + 4 adds the border to only one side (outer side x + 2). 16 comes from squaring (x + 4) as x2 + 16, which leaves out the middle term. 2x2 + 8x + 16 adds the photo area instead of subtracting it.

The hourly charges are $12 for the kayak and $3 for the life jacket: 12h + 3h = 15h.

Total: 20 + 15h.

items.prompt:
Evaluate the expression when x = −2 and y = 3.

−x2 + 5xy

mistakes.why: You treated −x<sup>2</sup> as +4. Square first, then apply the negative: −(−2)<sup>2</sup> = −4.
You made 5xy positive. 5(−2)(3) = −30, so −4 − 30 = −34.
You made both parts positive. −(−2)<sup>2</sup> = −4 and 5(−2)(3) = −30.

Substitute: −(−2)2 + 5(−2)(3)

Exponent: (−2)2 = 4, so −(−2)2 = −4

Multiply: 5(−2)(3) = −30

Add: −4 + (−30) = −34

items.prompt:
Simplify: 5 − 3(2x − 4) + 7x

Type your answer like 2x + 7.

mistakes.why: You made −3 × (−4) negative. A negative times a negative is positive: +12, so 5 + 12 = 17.
You subtracted 5 − 3 first and distributed 2. Distributing comes before subtracting: −3(2x − 4) = −6x + 12.
You added 6x and 7x. The distributed term is −6x, so −6x + 7x = x.

items.explain:
Distribute −3: −3 × 2x = −6x and −3 × (−4) = +12

Rewrite: 5 − 6x + 12 + 7x

Combine: −6x + 7x = x, and 5 + 12 = 17

Answer: x + 17

Check x = 1: 5 − 3(−2) + 7 = 18, and 1 + 17 = 18. If you got 11x − 8, you subtracted 5 − 3 before distributing.

items.prompt:

The result can be written as 3x2 + bx + 6. What is the value of b?

You added 3 and 7 and dropped the sign of −3x. After flipping, the x terms are −3x + 7x = 4x.

items.explain:
Flip every sign in the second polynomial: 8x2 − 3x + 2 − 5x2 + 7x + 4

x2 terms: 3x2. x terms: −3x + 7x = 4x. Constants: 2 + 4 = 6

Result: 3x2 + 4x + 6, so b = 4. If you got −10, the sign of −7x was not flipped.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (x − 7)(2x + 3)?
why: You multiplied only the first terms and the last terms. The outer product (3x) and inner product (−14x) are missing.
You reversed the signs of the middle products. Outer: x × 3 = 3x. Inner: −7 × 2x = −14x. Together: −11x.
You made the outer product negative. x × 3 = +3x, so 3x − 14x = −11x.
items.explain:
First: x × 2x = 2x2. Outer: x × 3 = 3x. Inner: −7 × 2x = −14x. Last: −7 × 3 = −21

Combine: 3x − 14x = −11x. Answer: 2x2 − 11x − 21

items.skill: Factoring trinomials and difference of squares
items.prompt:
Complete each statement.

x2 + 3x − 28 = (x + 7) × {{0}}

x2 − 25 = {{1}}

why: (x + 7)(x + 4) = x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 28. The last term must be −28, so one number is negative: 7 × (−4) = −28 and 7 + (−4) = 3.
(x + 7)(x − 7) = x<sup>2</sup> − 49. That is a difference of squares, not this trinomial; the numbers must multiply to −28.
(x + 7)(x + 21) = x<sup>2</sup> + 28x + 147. You looked for a number that adds to 7 to make 28. The two numbers must multiply to −28 and add to 3: 7 and −4.
(x − 5)² = x² − 10x + 25. It has a middle term and a +25. A difference of squares factors as a sum times a difference.
(x + 5)² = x² + 10x + 25. It has a middle term and a +25. x² − 25 needs (x + 5)(x − 5), whose middle terms cancel.

items.explain:
First statement: the numbers multiply to −28 and add to 3: 7 and −4. So x2 + 3x − 28 = (x + 7)(x − 4). Check: x2 − 4x + 7x − 28 = x2 + 3x − 28.

Second statement: x2 − 25 = x2 − 52, a difference of squares: (x + 5)(x − 5).

The most tempting wrong choice is (x − 5)², which gives x2 − 10x + 25.

items.prompt: Which expression shows 4x3 − 36x factored completely?
why: This is equivalent to 4x3 − 36x (multiply it back and you get the original), but it is not factored completely: x2 − 9 = x2 − 32 is a difference of squares, so it still factors as (x + 3)(x − 3).

This is equivalent to 4x<sup>3</sup> − 36x, but it stops two steps short. You factored out 4 and missed the common x: x<sup>3</sup> − 9x still has the factor x, so the GCF is 4x. After that, x<sup>2</sup> − 9 still factors as (x + 3)(x − 3).

4x(x − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 4x(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 9), which has a middle term, so it is not even equivalent to 4x<sup>3</sup> − 36x. A difference of squares factors as a sum times a difference: (x + 3)(x − 3).
items.explain:
GCF: both terms share 4 and x, so 4x3 − 36x = 4x(x2 − 9).

Difference of squares: x2 − 9 = x2 − 32 = (x + 3)(x − 3).

Completely factored: 4x(x + 3)(x − 3).

“Factored completely” means no factor can be factored any further. 4x(x2 − 9) and 4(x3 − 9x) are both equivalent to 4x3 − 36x, so they are not wrong math, but each still contains a factor that can be broken down: x2 − 9 is a difference of squares, and x3 − 9x still has a common factor of x. 4x(x − 3)2 is not equivalent at all; it has a middle term of −24x2 when multiplied out.

items.prompt:
A rectangular room is (2x + 1) feet long and (x + 3) feet wide. A rectangular closet in one corner measures x feet by 2 feet and will not be carpeted.

mistakes.why: You found the area of the whole room, 13 × 9 = 117, and did not subtract the closet (6 × 2 = 12).
You added the closet area instead of subtracting it: 117 + 12. The closet is not carpeted, so subtract it.
You multiplied only the first terms and the last terms, so the room came out as 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3 = 75 instead of 117, and 75 − 12 = 63. The room area is (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 2x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 3.

Room: (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 2x2 + 6x + x + 3 = 2x2 + 7x + 3

Closet: 2x

Carpeted area: 2x2 + 7x + 3 − 2x = 2x2 + 5x + 3

When x = 6: 2(36) + 5(6) + 3 = 72 + 30 + 3 = 105 square feet

Check with the dimensions: the room is 13 ft by 9 ft (117 sq ft), the closet is 6 ft by 2 ft (12 sq ft), and 117 − 12 = 105.

items.prompt:
Complete each statement.

x2 − 7x + 12 = (x − 3) × {{0}}

why: (x − 3)(x + 4) = x<sup>2</sup> + x − 12. The last term must be +12, so both numbers are negative: (−3)(−4) = 12 and −3 + (−4) = −7.
(x − 3)(x − 9) = x<sup>2</sup> − 12x + 27. You looked for a number that adds to −3 to make −12. The two numbers must multiply to 12 and add to −7: −3 and −4.

Second statement: x2 − 64 = x2 − 82, a difference of squares: (x + 8)(x − 8).

mistakes.why: You found the area of the whole poster, 17 × 9 = 153, and did not subtract the photo (5 × 5 = 25).

You multiplied only the first terms and the last terms, so the poster came out as 3x<sup>2</sup> + 8 = 83 instead of 153, and 83 − 25 = 58. The poster area is (3x + 2)(x + 4) = 3x<sup>2</sup> + 14x + 8.

Photo: 5x

Uncovered area: 3x2 + 14x + 8 − 5x = 3x2 + 9x + 8

vocab.def: A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
vocab.example: In 25m + 40, m is the variable (number of months).

vocab.def: A combination of numbers, variables, and operations, with no equal sign.
One part of an expression, separated from the others by + or − signs; the sign in front belongs to the term.
The number multiplied by a variable in a term.
A term with no variable; its value does not change.
Terms with exactly the same variable part, including exponents. Only like terms can be combined.
vocab.example: 4x and −9x are like terms; 3x and 3x<sup>2</sup> are not.

vocab.def: To find the value of an expression by substituting numbers for the variables.
Multiplying a number by a sum means multiplying it by each term: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
One term or a sum of terms in which variables have whole-number exponents.
Polynomials with one, two, and three terms.
A memory aid for multiplying two binomials: First, Outer, Inner, Last.
To write an expression as a product; also, each of the expressions being multiplied.
The largest number and highest power of each variable that divide every term.
A perfect square minus a perfect square; it factors as a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup> = (a + b)(a − b).
A polynomial written with its terms in order from the highest exponent to the lowest, with the constant last.
vocab.example: 6 − 2x + x<sup>2</sup> in standard form is x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 6.

notes:
Week 7 Study Sheet: Algebraic Expressions

Words to Math

WordsMath
8 more than nn + 8
5 less than nn − 5
twice n, decreased by 32n − 3
twice the sum of n and 32(n + 3)
n divided by 4n/4

Cost = flat fee + rate × amount (e.g., 40 + 25m)

Perimeter = sum of all sides; rectangle P = 2l + 2w

Evaluate and Simplify

  • Substitute in parentheses: x = −3 → x2 = (−3)2 = 9
  • Like terms: same variable, same exponent. 7x − 2x = 5x; 3x + 2 stays.
  • Distribute to every term: −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10
  • −(a − b) = −a + b

Example: 4(2x − 3) − 2(x − 5) = 8x − 12 − 2x + 10 = 6x − 2

Polynomials

  • Add: combine like terms.
  • Subtract: flip every sign in the second, then combine.
  • Multiply: every term × every term. FOIL: First, Outer, Inner, Last.
  • x × x = x2; 3x × 2x2 = 6x3

(x + 4)(3x − 2) = 3x2 − 2x + 12x − 8 = 3x2 + 10x − 8

(x + 3)2 = x2 + 6x + 9 (not x2 + 9)

Factoring Checklist

  1. GCF first: 8x3 + 12x2 = 4x2(2x + 3)
  2. Trinomial x2 + bx + c: two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. x2 + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3)
  3. Difference of squares: a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b). x2 − 49 = (x + 7)(x − 7)
  4. Factor completely: 2x2 − 32 = 2(x + 4)(x − 4)
  5. Check by multiplying back.

GED strategy — plug in a number: to test whether two expressions are equivalent, evaluate both at x = 2 (avoid 0 and 1). Equivalent expressions give the same value. Check factoring by multiplying back out.

Top mistakes: distributing to only the first term; flipping only one sign when subtracting; combining unlike terms; forgetting parentheses around negative values; writing 5 − n for “5 less than n”; stopping before factoring completely.
